body:
CHANGELOG updated in LO: Wrote LO_2D_NORTHSTAR.md: a real, rigorous, design-only bidirectional 2D grid execution model for LO (SECTION 549, founder real-time: 'make LO work both left to right and bottom to top... resolve at the same time... matrix of emojis... dominoes crossroads... its like lisp the actual programming language is data'). Chosen model: a checkerboard grid (operand cells even/even, row-ops even/odd, col-ops odd/even, reserved corners odd/odd) resolved by worklist fixed-point iteration over a dependency graph, not any fixed traversal order -- justified via confluence (any resolution order reaches the same result), with rejected alternatives named (sequential row-then-column, unspecified nondeterministic order, a general constraint solver, always-self-verifying literals). Shared 'junction' cells (new glyph 🧩) require both axes to independently supply a value and pass an EQ-check -- agreement resolves the cell, disagreement is a compile-time 'dominoes don't fit' error, never a runtime guess. Four full hand-derived worked examples, including a real junction-mismatch case (changing one literal three cells away breaks a downstream crossroads). Honest .prn mapping: needs a brand-new compile-time elaboration pass (the one genuinely new piece of engineering, doesn't exist anywhere in LO/PARENA/BURROW today) that erases the grid to an ordinary Let-chain before PARENA ever sees it -- reaches parena build only, not burrow build (no let support there), same already-documented boundary. Checked PARENA/STDLIB.md directly for the homoiconic angle: PARENA's own general Vec-of-Vec already exists, so the real remaining gap for a runtime-inspectable grid is on qi's frontend side, not a PARENA stdlib gap. Five open questions named explicitly, not guessed at. Updated NORTHSTAR.md (cross-link + Related) and README.md (Status: design only, not implemented) per README Reality. Registered LO-2D-NORTH in EMILY/context/golden-docs-index.md. No compiler code written -- design only, matching the item's own scoping. (sess-20260923-1030-4a526255)

⚓ ☃
